name: Brahmi

historicalPeriod.text: Attested from the third century BCE until the late first millennium CE.

geographicDistribution.text: A historical script of India, whose many regional varieties ultimately became the modern Indian writing systems.

characteristics.text: The Asokan rock inscription at Girnar is written in the Brahmi alphabet.
Bharhut inscriptions are edited as part of the work on early Brahmi inscriptions, and their letters were compared with those of Asoka's time.

relationships.text: Described, with Kharoshthi, as ultimately of Semitic origin, probably deriving from Aramaic. The source hedges this.

limitations: The sources read do not state a writing direction, so none is given here.
Regional and later forms differ from the early forms used in this research scope.
